title: He was beaten by police for leading a protest. His death radicalized the generation that followed him. November 17, 2026.
excerpt: On the 98th anniversary of his death, the story of Lala Lajpat Rai - "Punjab Kesari" - whose death after a police lathi-charge pushed a new generation of revolutionaries toward independence.
bodyHtml:
He was beaten by police for leading a protest. His death radicalized the generation that followed him

Lala Lajpat Rai died on November 17, 1928, from injuries sustained in a police lathi-charge. Known as "Punjab Kesari" - the Lion of Punjab - Rai was leading a protest against the Simon Commission in Lahore on October 30, 1928, when police charged the demonstrators. He died 18 days later from his injuries.

His death pushed a new generation of revolutionaries toward direct action. Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev - then young revolutionaries - held the police officer they blamed for Rai's death responsible, an episode that marked a turning point in their path toward the independence movement's more militant wing.

Lajpat Rai didn't live to see independence - but the anger his death provoked became part of the momentum that eventually got the country there.
